key_insight: The paper turns Gauss--Newton into a tensor-compressed, operator-aware second-order optimizer for PINNs, exploiting separable PDE structure to avoid the full tensor-product Jacobian.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster and more accurate training for high-dimensional parametric PDE solvers, making PINNs more practical for large-scale scientific computing.
method: Use the Gauss--Newton pullback metric to build curvature-aware updates in parameter space.
Exploit coordinate-separable neural architectures and finitely separable linearized PDE operators to factor the residual Jacobian exactly.

Compress the resulting linear system with canonical polyadic or tensor-train structure, so the reduced problem depends on local grid sizes and contraction patterns rather than the full collocation grid.
evidence_signal: Experiments on high-dimensional and parametric PDEs show lower errors than tensor-compressed first-order baselines, with orders-of-magnitude fewer iterations and only a fraction of the compute time.
watch_item: The approach relies on strong separability assumptions and careful tensor contraction design, so performance and scalability may degrade if the PDE/operator or architecture is not sufficiently separable.
paper_title: Tensor-Train Compressed Separable PINNs: A Curvature-Aware Optimization Framework for Parametric PDEs in High Dimensions
